method: Direct visual inspection of the 15 saved Godot PNGs through view_image. This is a subjective assistant still-image review, not human playtesting or continuous-motion acceptance.
criteria: Distinct and cohesive visual identities for all three new arenas
Readable platform tops and four fighters in normal High/Low fixtures
No obvious missing textures, intrusive opaque blockout scenery or prior Ember coplanar-face pattern in the inspected stills
High and low recovery identities remain within the visible game area
Intentionally overlapping player labels remain separated and readable
observations: Low deliberately simplifies scenery; Ember retains mounting hardware and chains after ornamental gears and vessels are hidden.
Extreme recovery fixtures produce small character images; labels preserve identity, while actual continuous tracking remains a separate validation scope.
limitations: No continuous animation, temporal flicker, attack effects, hazard timing, audio, gameplay balance or frame pacing is established by this still review.
No human or physical-controller playtest was performed.
This review covers these exact image hashes, not later runtime changes or an exported build.

views.findings: Jungle vista, stone top planes and all four fighter silhouettes read clearly. The center platform fits below the timer; no opaque scenery blocks the central fighting area.
Reduced foliage/detail and simpler surfaces preserve the same recognizable setting, top edges, fighter visibility and HUD layout.
The forced distant launch and low recovery both remain visible with player labels; margin foliage does not obscure the low fighter.
Both low recovering fighters are visible outside the deck sides. Roots and leaves leave the recovery lanes readable.
All four intentionally overlapping identities have separated readable labels; the models intentionally share the same fixture position.
Pale gallery and brass frame separate from the deep blue ocean. Four fighters and all top planes remain legible; restrained marine detail does not cover the fighting lane.
Removed caustics/detail visibly reduce fidelity but preserve the clean gallery silhouette, scene identity, labels and playable ledges.
Wide camera includes both the high launch and low recovering fighter. The arch remains background framing without hiding the tested fighters.
Both low fighters remain visible in front of or beside the outer columns, with labels and deck side boundaries readable.
Four separated identity labels remain readable over the decorative arch, while the deliberately overlapping bodies remain centered in frame.

The forge backdrop remains unobstructed; small gears and banded vessels fit the margins. Four fighters, glowing deck ends and inset platform tops are readable. Previous competing bronze/top-face patterns are absent in this still.
The forge setting and top-plane silhouettes remain clear after decorative gears, vessels and rivets are removed. Structural mounting posts and chains remain as lower-detail scenery.
Both extreme fighters and their labels remain visible in the expanded view. No flat foreground lava plane obscures the forge depths or the recovery area.
Both low recoveries remain visible beneath the deck edges; chains and crucibles do not hide the tested fighters or their labels.
All four intentionally overlapping identities have separate readable labels near the crown; the inset bronze surround appears clean in the captured view.
